title: Exposure Syllabus: Guided Rollout Journey and Compact Decision Cards
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Design a compact, beginner-friendly 'Exposure Syllabus' flow inside Redwood Console that guides engineers and PMs through staged rollouts (canary -> A/B -> staged split) while surfacing cost and rollback trade-offs in one glance.

Scope: prototype a two-screen flow + a collapsible decision-card component that plugs into existing Rollouts canvas: (1) Guided Syllabus stepper with suggested defaults and rationale, (2) Decision Cards drawer with quick actions (pause, accelerate, rollback, snapshot telemetry).

Primary success metrics: reduce time-to-first-safe-rollout by 30% for new teams; decrease accidental full-traffic launches (post-mortem flagged) by 50%; usability SUS >= 75 in targeted researcher sessions.

Design constraints & principles:
- Start simple: present a single recommended path with opt-out advanced controls.
- Default safe behavior: short canary (5% for 15m), verify telemetry anchors, then staged ramp.
- Make rollback visible and actionable: one-click rollback snapshot and reason capture.
- Surface approximate cost impact per step in-line (est. $/1000 requests) without hiding the performance trade-offs.
- Respect privacy: no PII in default telemetry preview.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Cognitive load vs configurability: we reduced the number of knobs on the primary syllabus stepper; advanced settings live behind an 'Expert mode' toggle to avoid overwhelming early adopters.
- Real-time telemetry vs noise: prototype shows 3 anchored signals (latency p50, error rate, qualitative NPS for feature) instead of a full dashboard to avoid alert fatigue.

Deliverables in this ticket: 
- High-fidelity prototype (figma + clickable InVision) for two syllabus states (fresh rollout, in-progress rollout).
- Decision Card component spec (variants, states, microcopy, a11y notes).
- Interaction spec for quick rollback and for cost-awareness tooltip.
- Usability test plan with 8 sessions and acceptance criteria.

Integration / Handoffs: 
- Engineering will implement Decision Card as an embeddable react component. Signal names & telemetry hooks: see ENG integration doc (attachments).
- PM to validate recommended defaults against current fleet telemetry and SLA policies.

Notes on novelty: this flow intentionally reframes 'traffic splitting' as an educational syllabus with explicit learning checkpoints and a 'confidence meter' that aggregates signal health and cost delta to recommend next step.
comments: 2025-11-05 - Kickoff: Reviewed scope with PM (Lena Zhou) and SRE (Riley Carter). PM asked for explicit SLA guardrail integration; SRE requested a strict default cap for ramp velocity.

2025-11-07 - Iteration 1 uploaded to Figma. Engineering flagged complexity of telemetry anchors; decided to limit to 3 signals and expose a configurator API for advanced telemetry mapping (ENG-88221 dependency).

2025-11-10 - Usability draft: three internal sessions with solutions engineers. Key feedback: decision cards are useful but language for 'cost impact' needs contextual examples. Updated microcopy and added cost delta examples to prototype.

2025-11-12 - Design review with Console UX: recommended adding keyboard-accessible quick rollback and clarify the rollback reason flow so it maps to audit logs. Added accessibility checklist to Decision Card spec.

2025-11-15 - Engineering review: agreed to implement 'snapshot + rollback' as a guarded action requiring two confirmations and a short free-text reason to populate audit logs (security_review_required=true in parent PM ticket).
2025-11-17 - This ticket ready for final stakeholder review. Attached figma and confluence pages; requesting FE estimates and a small SRE integration spike to expose telemetry anchors in dev cluster.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable prototype demonstrates full syllabus flow from create -> canary -> staged ramp -> rollback with less than 4 clicks between major actions
Decision Card component spec includes states (idle, monitoring, alert, rollback-ready) and a11y keyboard patterns
Cost delta tooltip shows estimated $ delta and a short plain-language rationale for each step
Usability sessions (n=8) show 80% task success for 'set up a safe canary' and SUS >= 75
Engineering implementation plan and signal contract (ENG owner assigned) exist and are linked in attachments
